topic: Kubernetes services — ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer reference
linkedin_hook: Mastering Kubernetes services is crucial for any DevOps engineer, and I'm sharing my go-to cheatsheet to help you deploy like a pro!
linkedin_intro: As a senior DevOps engineer, I've worked with numerous Kubernetes clusters and services. I've compiled a comprehensive cheatsheet to help my fellow engineers navigate the complexities of ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer services. This cheatsheet is based on my real-world experience and is designed to be a practical reference guide.

pro_tips:
Use kubectl get svc -o wide to quickly identify the type and ports of your services
and use kubectl describe svc/nginx to get detailed information about a specific service.

Use kubectl patch svc/nginx -p='{"spec":{"type":"LoadBalancer"}}' to update a service to use a load balancer
and use kubectl get svc -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].hostname}' to retrieve the hostname of the load balancer.

Use kubectl annotate svc/nginx load-balancer.kubernetes.io/internal=true to configure a load balancer to be internal
and use kubectl get svc -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.externalTrafficPolicy}' to retrieve the external traffic policy of a service.

Use kubectl get ep to list all endpoints in the current namespace
and use kubectl get pod -o wide to list all pods in the current namespace with detailed information.
